---
title: "Errors and limitations"
subtitle: "How a message reads, what a slide record carries, and what is specified but not implemented."
description: "The error grammar every Lanterne message follows, the slide record the renderer reads, and the limitations of the current development state."
---

## How an error reads

Every validation in the package routes through `src/utils/errors.typ`, so every message has the same grammar:

```text
<scope>: <problem>; got <repr(value)>. <hint>
```

`<scope>` is the function the author called, not the helper that raised the error: a token rejected on behalf of `theme-tokens` names `theme-tokens`.
Typst cannot catch a panic, so every one of these is a compile error rather than something a deck can recover from.

Three shapes cover the failures:

Enumerated values

: `deck: aspect-ratio must be one of "16-9", "4-3"; got "21-9".`

Types and shapes

: `theme-tokens: bg must be a colour; got 1.`

Everything else

: `slide-options must come before the slide's content. Move the slide-options call to just after the heading.`

`tests/expect-fail/` is the authoritative list of what each guard rejects: one file per case, each carrying the exact message it must produce.
A guard cannot be exercised from inside a unit test, because Typst cannot catch a panic, so those cases compile files that are asserted to fail.

## The slide record

Read from `src/core/record.typ`.
A record is the one dictionary a slide is described by, and is what the renderer reads.
It is not exported, and is documented here because it is the contract the machine surface will be built on.

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"content"` or `"section"` | A section slide is a divider, and must have a title. |
| `title` | content or `none` | The heading's body, describing the slide. |
| `level` | positive integer or `none` | The level that heading stands at. |
| `label` | label or `none` | The heading's label, carried because content equality ignores labels. |
| `attrs` | dictionary | Every slide option, each unnamed one at its default. |
| `body` | content | What renders, the opening heading included. |

: The slide record. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[12,25,63]"}

`title` and `level` stand or fall together: a title with no level describes a heading at no level, and a level with no title describes a heading that is not there.

There is no `layout` key.
Layouts arrive with the code that resolves them, and a key nothing reads is a key whose meaning no reader can check.

## What is not implemented

What is specified but not implemented, as of the current development state:

Content opacity

: Typst 0.15 has no content opacity, so `dim` and `focus` set the text fill of a dimmed region rather than fading it. An image, an explicit fill and a stroke inside a dimmed region do not dim.

Counters and chrome that read a step

: A progress bar and a slide number that read the step index arrive with the renderer slots. A figure, a block equation and a footnote already keep their numbers across the steps of a slide, and a footnote inside a hidden region makes no entry until it is revealed: it is replaced by a mark of the same width, so a footnote inside a container of your own needs that container registered.

Layouts and chrome

: A slide is its title and its body. There is no header, footer, progress indicator, slide number or logo, and no layout system to place them.

The element catalogue

: Callouts, columns and the rest of the structural elements are not implemented.

Reconstruction of unknown elements

: The traversal refuses, loudly, to rebuild an element it has no registry entry for, rather than guessing. A deck that silently lost a step boundary is worse than one that failed to build. `notes/roundtrip-findings.md` records which elements were characterised and how.

Markers inside `context`

: A marker inside a `context` block is invisible to the traversal, because a context block reports no fields until layout resolves it. Anything the traversal must see has to be written outside `context`.

Cross references by name

: A labelled heading is a link destination, so `#link(<label>)` works. Typst refuses `@label` on a heading that is not numbered, so write `#set heading(numbering: ...)` to reference a slide by name.

Labels on a stepped slide

: A slide's body is emitted once per step, so a label on it is dropped on every step but the one that keeps it, which is the first step where the element it marks is shown. A reference therefore lands where that element first appears. Three labels cannot be moved and are refused rather than dropped without a word: one on an image, which cannot be rebuilt, one on a stepped region itself, since the marker is replaced by what it resolves to, and one inside a container of your own that is not registered, which cannot be rebuilt either.

Headings and bookmarks on a stepped slide

: A slide's title is the heading the author wrote, and a stepped slide's body, heading included, is emitted once per step, so `query(heading)` returns it once per step. The outline and the bookmarks are not affected: a step page that repeats a slide carries `set heading(numbering: none, outlined: false, bookmarked: false)`, so the slide is listed once and bookmarked once however many steps it has. A section slide is a bookmark, a content slide is not, and an appendix slide is neither.

A `set heading(offset: ...)` rule

: A heading's level is read from the heading itself, under whichever of `level`, `depth` and `offset` the author reached for. An offset set by a rule lives in the style wrapper, and Typst exposes no way to read a wrapper's rules, so such a heading splits at the level it was written at rather than the level it renders at. Write the level you mean, or set `slide-level` to match the offset. An `offset` passed to `heading` itself is a field, so it is read and counted.
